summary.headline: MGL Q2 FY27 EBITDA fell to INR287 crore from INR343 crore QoQ as West Asia-driven industrial curtailments and costs weighed; volumes rose 2.6% QoQ to 4.89 MMSCMD.
summary.overview: Total sales volume rose to 4.892 MMSCMD in Q2 from 4.766 MMSCMD in Q1 (up 2.63% QoQ, 6.49% YoY), led by CNG and DPNG. Profitability weakened: EBITDA from operations was INR287 crore versus INR343 crore in Q1, and PAT was INR137 crore versus INR194 crore. H1 EBITDA was INR630 crore (vs INR839 crore in H1 FY26) and H1 PAT was INR331 crore (vs INR513 crore). Management attributed the squeeze to volume-linked costs, a one-time actuarial/pay-revision charge of about INR10-12 crore, and gas sourcing costs tied to the West Asia conflict and HPHT allocation changes.

segments.name: CNG
segments.commentary: Volume 3.552 MMSCMD in Q2 with 29,524 vehicles added in the quarter, taking registered CNG vehicles above 1.34 million; 528 CNG stations after adding 9. Gas mix about 60% domestic (APM/NWG ~40%, HPHT ~40% including IGX), 40% term and ~4% spot.

segments.name: Domestic PNG (DPNG)
segments.commentary: Volume 0.639 MMSCMD; 70,501 conversions in the quarter, cumulative 2.24 million as of 30 September 2026. Sourced 100% from APM gas.

segments.name: Industrial & commercial (I&C)
segments.commentary: Volume 0.70 MMSCMD, down 7.48% YoY on RLNG supply curtailment (around 70-80% of requirement) and high Brent; small commercial (LPG-substitute) volumes up about 9-10%. Customers: 6,409, with 248 added in the quarter. Realisations ranged INR65 to above INR100 per unit depending on customer and fuel mix.

segments.name: Infrastructure
segments.commentary: Laid 65 km of steel and PE pipeline in the quarter, taking total network above 8,500 km.

guidance_outlook: Management expects volume growth to exceed 8-9% in both FY27 and FY28 once industrial gas supply and pricing normalise; Ajay Sinha said 9-10% sales volume growth is being delivered and hoped to sustain it in FY28.
Capex guidance of INR1,500-1,800 crore maintained for FY27, with H1 run rate lower due to monsoon pipeline-laying restrictions; work expected to pick up from October.

Operating cash flow expected at INR1,000-1,200 crore; operating cash flow less capex likely negative by INR200-300 crore in FY27-28. Management said debt is not warranted given around INR1,000 crore surplus.

HPHT allocation formula phasing: 25% weight on past consumption in Nov-Dec 2026, 50% Jan-Mar 2027, 75% Apr-Jun 2027, 100% from July 2027. Management expects HPHT allocation to rise from about 5,000-6,000 MMBtu/day to 16,000-18,000 MMBtu/day at full implementation, if monthly IGX flows hold.
Management does not give EBITDA margin guidance for FY27 or FY28, citing volatility; it said a INR1-1.5/SCM CNG price increase could lift unit EBITDA to about INR7/SCM, all else equal.
capex_capacity: H1 FY27 capex about INR643 crore against FY27 guidance of INR1,500-1,800 crore; management says it still aims for INR1,500 crore-plus and cites constraints on manpower and materials.
Pipeline network above 8,500 km after 65 km added in Q2; 9 CNG stations added to reach 528.
Spot LNG about 4% of CNG volume (about 2.5% of company volume); including HPHT exchange spot via IGX, about 11% of company volume.
Around 40,000 MMBtu/day of new term RLNG signed, already flowing, mainly Henry Hub-linked with a smaller Brent-linked portion; take-or-pay thresholds apply.
Large CNG commercial vehicle incentive scheme: 800+ vehicles committed, around 110 delivered in Q2 at about INR3.5 lakh each (INR3.5-4 crore spend). LCV incentives discontinued.
demand_pricing: Customer-level pricing for I&C is reset monthly on alternate-fuel formulas (LPG 19 kg, FO, LDO, Brent-linked); management says there is no change in pricing strategy.
LPG cylinder prices rose more than 25% QoQ in Q2 while LDO and FO fell about 6-15%, so realisation rose for LPG-linked commercial customers and fell for FO/LDO-linked industrial customers.
CNG discount to petrol about 45% (ethanol-blended petrol basis) and about 10-11% to diesel, held for a long period; management says it wants to protect CNG adoption.
Industrial/large customers are about 78-80% of I&C volume by management's estimate: 20-22% small customers and the balance large industrial customers.
LNG spot prices were in a $22-23 per MMBtu range during the quarter; NWG pricing is seen as close to RLNG/term prices, prompting calls for an NWG allocation policy with priority for CNG.

qa_highlights.question: What share of volume was spot LNG and at what price?
qa_highlights.answer: Spot was about 4% of CNG volume and about 2.5% of company volume; with HPHT exchange spot via IGX it was about 11%. LNG was around $22-23 per MMBtu.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for CNG margins and unit EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 unit EBITDA was about INR6.77/SCM; INR1-1.5/SCM of price increase would take it to about INR7 if costs are unchanged. No FY27/28 margin guidance given.

qa_highlights.question: Why did operating expenses rise and was there a one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume-linked costs (power, fuel, LCV transport, dispensing) rose, and a one-time actuarial impact of about INR10-12 crore from the pay revision was booked in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Why did I&C volumes decline and when will they recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Industrial volumes fell on RLNG curtailment (about 70-80% supply) and high Brent; management expects double-digit recovery once conditions normalise. Small commercial volumes grew 9-10%.

qa_highlights.question: Will capex guidance hold and how will the negative FCF be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex guidance of INR1,500-1,800 crore holds; FCF is negative INR200-300 crore, funded from about INR1,000 crore surplus and INR1,000-1,200 crore operating cash flow; no debt planned, with some funding from customer deposits.

qa_highlights.question: What is the new HPHT allocation rule and volume impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Allocation shifts from equal per-entity sharing to consumption-weighted, phased in fully from July 2027. MGL's allocation is expected to rise from 5,000-6,000 MMBtu/day to 16,000-18,000 MMBtu/day at full implementation.

qa_highlights.question: Was there a penalty for UEPL MWP shortfall at takeover?
qa_highlights.answer: PNGRB asked for MWP shortfall recovery at takeover; the JV agreement covered recovery from erstwhile promoters, with a nominal amount borne by MGL post takeover.

risks_watch: RLNG supply curtailment (around 70-80%) and volatile LNG and Brent prices, which weigh on industrial volumes and realisations.
HPHT allocation phase-in: volumes depend on monthly IGX flows, and term contracts may be split into pre- and post-June 2027 portions.
Unit EBITDA is about INR6.77/SCM against a INR7 benchmark; monitor whether CNG price revisions are made and how they affect vehicle adoption given the discount to petrol and diesel.
Negative FCF of INR200-300 crore in FY27-28 with no planned debt; watch cash balance and customer deposit funding.
Capex execution risk from manpower and material constraints across CGD players.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volume growth and long-term demand, but cautious and non-committal on margins, citing volatile gas costs and supply. Management was evasive on FY27-28 EBITDA guidance and on NWG allocation policy, and explained the margin dip with volume-linked costs and one-offs.
key_quotes: Gas supplies to industrial and commercial customers are partly curtailed.
So, the sign contract and normal level consumption during normal if -- restores, our growth will be definitely more than 8% to 9% for both the years.
The results have been better we feel than the market expectations.
Debt may not get warranted as such because I have still surplus of almost INR1,000 crores.

growth.why: Management reiterates CNG volume growth of more than 8-9% in both FY27 and FY28 and holds FY27 capex at INR1,500-1,800 crore, but H1 capex of INR643 crore is well behind that run rate, and the guidance is backed by a 65 km pipeline addition, 9 new stations and new term RLNG rather than large capacity additions.
